Rüegg MA.role: Neurobiologist at the Biozentrum of the University of Basel who studies how muscles and the nerve connections that drive them develop, age and fail, and a co-author on three early mouse and cell studies that mapped what mTORC1 and mTORC2 do in muscle, fat and liver
Rüegg MA.sub: Professor of Neurobiology, Biozentrum, University of Basel · Co-founder and CEO, SEAL Therapeutics (since 2021) · Postdoctoral fellow, Stanford University (1989–1992)
story: Markus Rüegg is a middle author on three Atlas studies from the Biozentrum in Basel, all done together with Michael Hall's group. In 2004, the group showed in mouse cells that a second mTOR complex, mTORC2, exists. It is not blocked by rapamycin and helps control the actin cytoskeleton, the protein scaffold that gives a cell its shape. In 2008, mice that lacked raptor, a key part of mTORC1, only in fat tissue stayed lean and burned more energy in their mitochondria. In 2012, mice that lacked rictor, a key part of mTORC2, only in the liver could not switch the liver from making glucose to using it after a meal, and they developed high blood sugar and low blood fats.

The Biozentrum website lists Rüegg as full professor of neurobiology at the University of Basel since 2004, after earlier posts there as assistant and associate professor. He studied biochemistry at the University of Zurich and worked as a postdoctoral fellow in the neurobiology department at Stanford University School of Medicine from 1989 to 1992. His group studies how the junction between nerve and muscle is built and kept up, muscle ageing and muscular dystrophies. The same group showed in 2008 that muscle without raptor becomes dystrophic, which is how mTORC1 entered his muscle work. Since 2021 he has also been co-founder and CEO of SEAL Therapeutics. His part in the Atlas studies is as a co-author, and the Atlas findings come from mice and cultured cells, not from people.

highlights.JAC2004: Middle author of the paper that described mTORC2 in mammalian cells, together with Michael Hall and colleagues at the Biozentrum.
highlights.POL2008: Middle author of the paper showing that removing raptor from fat tissue makes mice lean.
highlights.HAG2012: Middle author of the paper showing that liver-specific loss of rictor disturbs how the liver handles glucose and fat.

Rüegg MA.note: Identity: PubMed gives affiliation only for the first author of the three Atlas papers (all Biozentrum, Basel). Chain evidence: PMID 19497867 shares Cybulski, Polak, Auwerx, Hall with POL2008 but lists affiliation only for the first author; PMID 23497627 lists Rüegg MA at Biozentrum and shares Lin S and Hall MN with JAC2004; PMID 19046572 lists Rüegg with Hall, Lin. The official Biozentrum CV (name, ORCID, Biozentrum position) closes the gap. For HAG2012 the only shared senior author in the chain papers is Hall, so that study rests on same given name, same lab head and same institution. Role, positions and ORCID come from the Biozentrum CV page; the Wikipedia page is a secondary source only and its dates (professor since 1998) differ from the CV (full professor 2004), so the CV was followed.
